title: AGM Action Game Maker release party thread - out now!

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:

September 30 Update: v1.1.0 out and free trial until the end of October!

Honestly I can prototype any 2d game without heavy menuing in less than 5-6 hours with pgm/agm its ease of use is incredibly simple if you have a bit of experience.
AGM because its built on Godot has a slightly more awkward order of operations particularly in getting projects up and running, animations etc.. but is still relatively simple.  So the learning curve is slightly steeper than PGM but nothing you won't have down with of practice.
They are both a step up in terms of difficulty compared to RM but not nearly as complex as the alternatives like Game Maker (which itself has a low bar of entry and small learning curve).
Starbird_Resources said:
will this be available standalone or only through Steam?
Click to expand...
I've only been given access to a Steam version for beta testing so no idea if there will be an actual standalone sorry.
----------------------------------------------------
In general and with my experiences so far in beta testing.
The approach to Action Game Maker has been much better imho.  First off Action Game Maker takes advantage of Godot and works with it, instead of as almost separate entities.
So for example with Unite, to take advantage of Unity you had to do shenanigans, AGM is literally Godot with a visual script add-on and some custom nodes.  Exactly what many people wanted from Unite.
If I had to compare I would say AGM is closer to something like Ork Framework for Unity, than Unite.
My experience in the beta has been positive.  Bugs are quickly noted and patched asap, communication with the testers from the team is excellent.  They have been super helpful and the engine is a ton of fun and quick to create with.
They've also allowed us to stream, make videos etc... so the entire process has been really transparent.  I think people will be positively surprised at this one.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
padr81 said:
They are both a step up in terms of difficulty compared to RM but not nearly as complex as the alternatives like Game Maker
Click to expand...
It's been my experience people basically want prebuilt templates you can swap the assets of and don't like making anything from scratch. They like RPG Maker because there are already premade templates for the battle system, shop, menus, etc. and premade assets (the RTP). Just being easy to use and no code isn't enough. GDevelop does that, is cited as being one of the easiest engines on par with RPG Maker, and is still niche.
How much is prebuilt in AGM?
There's also cost. Godot is growing market share compared to its competitors because well... it's free. It's no coincidence people fled from Unity to Godot when Unity changed its pricing structure. AGM is $99.99, which puts it on price parity with Game Maker, who only charges you on the back end when you publish while AGM wants it upfront.

So there will be sample projects and some will be workable like that but to make anything meaningful you'll have to kind of combine and mix and match learning from sample in your own project.
I'm not sure how much I'm allowed to say on what's actually in there I'd have to check the agreement but there will be multiple around launch.
But where the engine really shines community wise is through a feature called modules.  Modules are basically Visual Script prefabs.   So if some creates a UI module, they can share it, it can be literally dragged into a project and will work exactly like a template with minor tweaking.
One thing I intend to do with my metroidvania tutorial series is eventually start sharing modules, like player controller module, basic enemy ai module etc..

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Update: Despite weak adoption GGG is still updating AGM and now has a weekly AGM newsletter. Sale price is now $79.99. The latest additions are another template and better collision detection.
IMO the biggest thing holding back adoption is the still high price. A lot of reviews balking at the price or some variant of "not worth it". Some cite bad UI or too difficult.
Interestingly enough GGG has their own RPG Maker forums that ONLY has AGM on it. Seems like it was made after they shut down the Unite forums and told everyone there to go to Discord.
RPG MAKER GUILD
The Official Community for Gotcha Gotcha Games Products
guild.rpgmakerofficial.com

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
♥SOURCE♥ said:
They said AGM is "
designed for users who are familiar with Godot but cannot code
," so presumably their target audience is too busy using whatever they were using before.
Click to expand...
It's pulled some Pixel Game Maker users looking to "upgrade", some RPG Maker users, and some Godot users. It's competing directly with the free Godot add-on Orchestrator and Visual Scripting extension. In addition it comes with some pre-built game templates and assets.
AGM does have some value but the market clearing price is likely significantly less than $80. It's hard to build on top a free engine, offer less than the base one and put a high price tag on it.
Addressing the value side instead of price, the UI and documentation needs more work. It's still not easy and intuitive enough. The engine is still buggy and not everything works properly.
